The bounding box of the level feature is expanded to include the
meaning: Which building level an indoor entry point sits on.

name: metadata
desc: Field-level metadata for this access point.
meaning: Bookkeeping metadata about this access point field.

name: point
desc: For access points to non-TYPE_SEGMENT features, the location of the access point. For access points to TYPE_SEGMENT features, this can be supplied as a fuzzy access point that is not guaranteed to be on the correct side of road. It should not be used by end clients in case of TYPE_SEGMENT access points.
meaning: The location of the entry point.

name: pointOffSegment
desc: If the access point is defined by a TYPE_SEGMENT feature, this is the location of the access point displaced slightly to the correct side of the segment. This offset is in a direction perpendicular to the direction of travel along the segment. The actual offset distance is unspecified. It would typically be relatively small (approximately 1 meter). You can subtract the "off segment" point from the "on segment" point to get a vector of unknown length pointing from "on seg
meaning: A point nudged to the correct side of the road from the entry point.

name: pointOnSegment
desc: If the access point is defined by a TYPE_SEGMENT feature, this is the point on the centerline of the segment that is closest to the actual access point. May be re-derived if necessary to maintain precise placement on segment.
meaning: The nearest point on the road centerline to the entry point.

name: priority
desc: LINT.ThenChange(//depot/google3/geostore/cleanup/callbacks/\ ID_DUPLICATE_ACCESS_POINT.cc)
meaning: A priority ordering value for this access point.

name: segmentPosition
desc: If the access point is defined by a TYPE_SEGMENT feature, this is the location of the access point expressed as a fractional distance along the segment. The value runs from 0 to 1 inclusive. May be re-derived if necessary to maintain precise placement on segment.
meaning: How far along the road segment the entry point sits, from 0 to 1.

name: unsuitableTravelMode
desc: This list represents the travel modes for which this access-point should be avoided. If this list is empty, the access-point is suitable for any travel mode. This is only used for access points to TYPE_SEGMENT features; access points to non-TYPE_SEGMENT features, e.g. TYPE_ESTABLISHMENT_POI features with gcid:transit_station GConcepts are just identified by feature_typ
meaning: Travel modes for which this entry point should not be used.

meaning: What kind of place this address part is, such as country or city.

meaning: The order of this address part among parts of the same kind.

meaning: The names given for this part of the address.

name: temporaryData

meaning: Scratch space for clients to attach data, never stored in the map data.

meaning: What kind of address part this is.

meaning: The language these address lines are written in.

meaning: Scratch space where clients can attach arbitrary data to an address; never set in live map data.

desc: Two or more address numbers. Each number represents an address that was mentioned by the data provider.

The parameters must be provided in increasing order and the values in the number array must be in strictl

desc: If specified, the prefix or suffix is applied to all numbers in the range. For example, this can be used to indicate that addresses B1 through B99 are on one side of the street, while A1 through A99 are on the other side of the street.
meaning: A letter or code applied to every address number in a range, such as the B in B1 through B99.

name: sameParity
desc: If 'same_parity' is true, then all 'number' values must have the same parity (even or odd), and this address range only includes addresses whose parity is the same as the given 'number' values.
meaning: Flag saying every address in the range is either even-numbered or odd-numbered.

name: temporaryData
desc: A place for clients to attach arbitrary data to an address range. Never set in MapFacts. We have future plans to make other changes so we can handle this case. Example #2: Single semi-numeric address (e.g., "12bis") The number array contains two copies of the single
meaning: Scratch space for arbitrary client data on an address range; never set in live map data.

desc: The ID to be used to fetch the feature’s geometry from the 3D Geometry Store.
meaning: Identifier used to fetch a map feature's 3D shape from the geometry store.

name: speedLimit

meaning: The speed limit value that applies to a road.

name: trustLevel
desc: The level of trust we have in this speed limit value.

desc: attachment_id distinguishes messages of the same type_id associated with the same feature. It can not be set to 0x0.

name: comment
desc: comment is a human-readable string that is logged whenever this attachment is processed by the framework.

name: messages
desc: messages contains the structured data for this attachment. It should contain a single message with a type ID matching the value of the type_id field below.
meaning: The structured payload carried by an attachment.

meaning: Pointer to the canonical attribute this attribute instance corresponds to.

meaning: Holds the attribute's value when that value is plain text.

name: locale
desc: The ID of the best-match TYPE_LOCALE feature for this feature.
meaning: Pointer to the locale feature that best matches this map feature.

desc: The ID of the localization policy to apply when selecting a name for a feature. This field should always be set. Localization policy IDs are arbitrary identifiers (up to some number of bytes; see geostore/base/public/constants.h) that uniquely distinguish a set of language-selection rules.
meaning: Id of the rule set used to pick which language name to show for a place.

name: metadata
desc: Field-level metadata for this best locale.
meaning: Field-level bookkeeping metadata for this best-locale record.

meaning: Per-domain overrides for how a border is displayed, required for legal reasons.

name: markerAdjacencyBeginFraction

meaning: Where along the marker's own line this association begins, as a fraction.

name: side
desc: Which side of the flowline does the marker occur on.
meaning: Which side of the lane the painted marker sits on.

meaning: Height of a building's base above ground level, in meters.

meaning: Rules for converting local vertex coordinates into real-world earth coordinates.

meaning: The color a 3D surface material shows under plain white light.

meaning: Local identifier for a 3D city object, unique only inside this record.

meaning: How detailed a 3D geometric representation is.

meaning: Geometry made of a single point, line, or loop.

name: semantics
desc: Predefined semantics that may be referenced from geometric primitives.

name: offered
desc: Represents if an item is offered at a business. For TYPE_JOB, this represents if this job is offered by the corresponding business
meaning: Whether the business actually offers this item or job.

name: price
desc: Price of the item. There should be at most one price for any given currency.
meaning: The price of an item, at most one entry per currency.

name: priceFormat
desc: Represents which price format is being used by this item, which determines the usage/meaning of the “price” field above. Optional – the default value is legal and safe (represents no price if the “price” field is unset).
meaning: Which price format the item uses, which decides how the price field is read.

name: rankingHint
desc: Numerical score which can be provided by data sources to indicate preferred item ordering. This is purely a hint – we are not required to followed it if we have a different order we think is better. Higher scores represent items that should be shown more prominently/earlier. Optional.
meaning: Provider-supplied score hinting which menu or product items should be shown first.

name: color
desc: Colors found on this crossing.
meaning: The colors painted on a pedestrian crossing.

name: pointCurvature
desc: Curvature values at points along the flowline. A linear interpolation between two successive points will yield the curvature value at intermediate points.
meaning: Curvature measurements at points along a road centerline.

name: controlPoint
desc: Internal Bezier handles. One can be used for a quadratic curve, two for cubic Beziers.
meaning: Control handles that define the shape of a curved road connection.

name: angleDegrees
desc: We use this parameterization to make curves change predictable when endpoints move. Each point P is defined in terms of the straight edge [S, E] between the start point of the curve S and its end point E.
meaning: Angle used to place a curve control point relative to the straight start-to-end line.

name: distanceMultiplier
desc: Distance(S, P) in units of Distance(S, E).
meaning: Distance of a curve control point from the start, measured in start-to-end lengths.

name: radius
desc: Arc radius. Must be greater than half-distance between two endpoints.
meaning: Radius of a circular arc connecting two road endpoints.

name: attributionUrl
desc: This is the URL of a website representing this DataSource as a whole. If this DataSource feature is specific to a particular dataset or product, the page may contain information relevant to that dataset or product or may be the main page of the organization.
meaning: Website address of the organization that supplied this map data.

name: copyrightOwner
desc: A UTF8 string that will be inserted in copyright messages to refer to this copyright owner, e.g. "Tele Atlas".
meaning: Name inserted into copyright notices for this map data source.

name: copyrightYear
desc: The copyright year of this data (which may be different than the year of the release date), e.g. 2005.
meaning: The copyright year of this map data.

name: description
desc: A free-form description of this data source. Ideally the description should include: - Where the data was obtained (URL, company name, individual, etc). - Where to find detailed documentation. - A brief summary of the licensing terms. - As much internal and external contact information as possible (e.g. who to ask about licensing questions, interpreting the data, updating the data, fixing bugs in the importer, etc).
meaning: Free-form notes on where map data came from, its licensing, and who to contact.

name: importerBuildInfo
desc: The build information of the importer binary used to generate this data source.
meaning: Build information for the binary that imported this data.

name: importerBuildTarget
desc: The build target of the importer binary used to generate this data source.
meaning: Build target of the binary that imported this data.

name: importerClientInfo
desc: The Perforce client information of the importer binary used to generate this data source.
meaning: Source-control client information for the importer binary.

name: importerMpmVersion
desc: If the importer was built as an MPM, the version number can be stored in this field. As with build_info, this can be useful when tracking down issues that may be due to the use of a particular binary.
meaning: Package version number of the importer binary.

name: importerTimestamp
desc: The timestamp of the importer binary used to generate this data source.
meaning: Timestamp of the importer binary used to generate this data.

name: provider
desc: The provider type of this data source.
meaning: What type of provider supplied this map data.

name: rawMetadata
desc: For every key that is used in raw_data from this source, there must be a corresponding entry in raw_metadata that describes this key.
meaning: Descriptions of every raw data key used by this map data source.

name: release
desc: A release string that doesn't have to be a date. This is provided so that we can preserve provider release strings that aren't based on dates. If you don't set it, the release_date will get formatted into this field for debugging purposes.
meaning: The provider's own release label, which need not be a date.

name: releaseDate
desc: The release date of this data.
meaning: The date this map data was released.

name: sourceDataset
desc: A data provider defined string describing the source dataset from which the features of this data source were generated. For example, the MultiNet "fra" dataset produces features for both France and Monaco.
meaning: The provider's name for the dataset these map features came from.

name: precision
desc: This attribute describes the precision of the date and time. It would be unusual for a data provider to provide a precision along with their date. It is more likely that the precision of a date will be inferred from the date format. For example "19th century" is likely to be correct to the century, while "1800" is probably correct to the year. The precision should be semantically interpreted as a cast, so a DateTimeProto object with a seconds value corresponding to 2018-03-28
meaning: How precise a stored date is, for example to the day, year, or century.

name: seconds
desc: Number of seconds since (or before) the UNIX epoch (January 1, 1970). This is also the standard epoch for Java and Python time representations. If it is important for this time be displayed correctly for different time zones, convert the time to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
meaning: A time stored as seconds before or after the Unix epoch.

name: displayLocation
desc: The location where this feature should be rendered.
meaning: The map location where this feature's label should be drawn.

name: administeredBy
desc: If present this feature is administered by the power present in the field. In most cases this will be a two letter ISO-3166 region code, but may be a descriptive string if no region code is available.
meaning: Which country or authority administers a disputed area.

name: claimant
desc: Feature IDs (usually a country feature ID) of all parties who claim this feature. No claimants means the claim by the country that contains it (based on country polygon) is not disputed.
meaning: The countries that claim a disputed area.

name: type
desc: The type of this feature -- see comments above.
meaning: The type of this doodle map feature.

name: isFree
desc: If true, represents that the rate is free; i.e. the price is 0 in any currency. If this is true, price must be empty.
meaning: Marks that a rate costs nothing in any currency.

name: periodicitySeconds
desc: The billable unit of the rate; i.e. after having utilized the service for exactly periodicity_seconds, the total cost should increase by ‘price’. For example, if the rate expresses a price per hour, then periodicity_seconds should be set to 3600. If this is unset, then the rate does not vary based on duration, and price represents a flat cost. May only be set if price is nonempty.
meaning: How many seconds of use one billing unit of the price covers.

name: price
desc: The total price, in each applicable currency, of utilizing the service for periodicity_seconds, or for the entire duration expressed by range_start_seconds and range_end_seconds if periodicity_seconds is 0. Each entry should have an ID of /measurement_unit/money_value and consist of two properties: one with an ID of /measurement_unit/money_value/amount and a float value with the amount, and another with the ID /measurement_unit/money_value/currency and an ID value with the MID of the proper curr
meaning: The price per billing period in each applicable currency.

name: rangeEndSeconds
desc: Upper bound for durations to match, exclusive. Unset implies indefinite.
meaning: Upper bound of the usage duration this rate applies to.

name: rangeStartSeconds
desc: Lower bound for durations to match, inclusive. Required; a value of 0 expresses that the price applies from the start of the utilization period.
meaning: Lower bound of the usage duration this rate applies to.

name: blendOrder
desc: Defines the relative order in which terrain data should be rendered. Features with higher blend_order should be blended on top of features with lower blend_order. NOTE: this is backwards from the way BlendRank works in Magrathean.
meaning: Order in which terrain layers should be drawn on top of one another.

name: dataLevel
desc: The zoom level at which this data is defined. Level 0 is world level data, and each increase in zoom level corresponds to a factor of 2 increase in scale.
meaning: The map zoom level at which this terrain data is defined.

name: dataMaxlevel
desc: The maximum (finest) level at which this terrain data has sufficient resolution to be displayed.
meaning: Finest zoom level at which this terrain data still has enough resolution.

name: elevationData
desc: A place to store an elevation data protocol buffer. Currently, this must be a keyhole::AssetTileCompressed (see google3/keyhole/common/proto/magrathean.protodevel).
meaning: Blob holding the compressed elevation data for a terrain tile.

name: fullChildDataAvailable
desc: If true, all of the data contained in this feature is available at the next highest (more detailed) level. If this is true, partial_child_data_available should also be true.
meaning: Flag that all of this tile's data also exists at the next zoom level.

name: partialChildDataAvailable
desc: If true, at least part of the data contained in this feature is available at the next highest (more detailed) level.
meaning: Flag that at least part of this tile's data exists at the next zoom level.

name: averageElevationMeters
desc: The average elevation of the feature in meters above the local mean sea level.
meaning: Average elevation of a place in meters above local sea level.

name: peak
desc: Additional details for TYPE_PEAK and TYPE_VOLCANO features.
meaning: Extra details for mountain peak and volcano features.

name: canEnter
desc: DEPRECATED. Please use enter_or_exit instead.
meaning: Deprecated flag for whether a place can be entered here; replaced by another field.

name: canExit
desc: Whether the target can be entered through this entrance. Whether the target can be exited through this entrance.
meaning: Whether a place can be entered or exited through this entrance.

name: featureId
desc: Feature ID of the related entrance. References should refer to TYPE_ENTRANCE or TYPE_COMPOUND features that are entrances or exits of the referencing feature.
meaning: Pointer to the entrance or exit feature belonging to this place.

name: bizbuilderReference
desc: Reference to BizBuilder data for this establishment. The bizbuilder_reference field indicates that a feature is claimed in CBDB (with the canonical state in MapFacts). The bizbuilder_reference is different from the social_reference's claimed_gaia_id because some BizBuilder clients will not have +Pages. All claimed businesses should have a bizbuilder_reference.
meaning: Link to business listing data showing the place has been claimed by its owner.

name: hours
desc: Regular opening hours for the establishment (weekly schedule).
meaning: The regular weekly opening hours of a business.

name: openingHours
desc: Opening hours for this establishment, including regular weekly hours and exceptional hours (e.g. on holidays). NOTE: in practice, only the exceptional hours are filled in this message. A schema migration for regular weekly hours was planned back in 2015 (see b/23105782) but was not completed and is (as of May 2018) not prioritized. Clients should continue getting regular opening hours from the
meaning: Opening hours including holiday exceptions; in practice only exceptions are filled in.

name: priceInfo
desc: Pricing for products and services offered. Example: menus for restaurants.
meaning: Prices for products and services offered, such as a restaurant menu.

name: telephone
desc: Telephone number and related information.
meaning: Phone numbers and related contact details for a business.

name: hours
desc: The weekly schedule to be applied for the dates that fall within the range. The schedule may contain hours only for days of the week that occur during the date range specified in the range field.
meaning: The replacement weekly schedule used during a special date range.

name: metadata
desc: Field-level metadata for this exception.
meaning: Field-level bookkeeping metadata for this hours exception.

name: range
desc: The dates for which this exception applies, expressed as a half open interval. For example, an exception that applies for the entire month of December 2015 should have a range December 1, 2015 to January 1, 2016. Any regular hours that start on days in this range are ignored and replaced by the exceptional hours for that day. The TimeIntervalProto for the range must be a fully specified, non-empty, and non-inverted range of dates. Concretely, the requirements are:
meaning: The date range over which special opening hours apply.

name: closeReason
desc: Structured reason for the permanent closure (if any).
meaning: Coded reason why a place closed permanently.

name: closed
desc: Indicates whether the place is closed (permanently or temporarily), i.e., not operational in the present, but was in the past. WARNING: New code should prefer go/geo-schema-reference:operational-status.
meaning: Whether a place has stopped operating, permanently or temporarily.

name: endAsOfDate
desc: The earliest known date of this feature's "end" (e.g. an establishment's permanent closure), if the actual date is unknown; i.e. the best known upper bound of the day end_date would represent. end_as_of_date must be in local (civil) time and of PRECISION_DAY. WARNING: Not necessarily consistent yet with
meaning: Earliest date by which a place was known to have closed, when the exact date is unknown.

name: removed
desc: Indicates whether the feature is marked as removed in the Geo repository. Removed features are still present in the Geo repository but are considered to be in an inactive state (not valid for lint purposes, not retrievable except explicitly by feature ID, etc.). NOTE: If you have access to a complete FeatureProto, do NOT read this bit directly to find out whether a feature is removed. Instead, rely on the IsFeatureRemoved() API, available in C++ (geostore/base/public/feature.h) and Java (geostor
meaning: Whether the map feature is flagged as inactive in the geo repository.

name: removedReason
desc: Structured reason why the feature is marked as removed. Relevant only when removed == true.
meaning: Coded reason why the map feature was marked removed.

name: startDate
desc: (Initial) start and (permanent) end dates of operations, such that start_date is the first day operational and end_date is the first day when operations have permanently ended. The only allowed precisions are PRECISION_DAY, PRECISION_MONTH, PRECISION_YEAR. DateTimeProto.seconds should have the lowest legal value for the desired date/time and precision. E.g. for PRECISION_MONTH, 2019-02-15 21:10:30 is not valid, it should be 2019-02-01 00:00:00 instead. NOTE: The start_date and end_date are store
meaning: The first day a place was operational.

name: fieldPath
desc: Represents all fields for which this SourceInfo is valid. NOTE: Field paths are rooted at FeatureProto level.
meaning: The set of field paths that a given source-information record covers.

name: featureBirthTimestampUs
desc: The timestamp (in microseconds since the UNIX epoch) when this feature first went live in the Geo repository. Note that this has no relation to the birth data of that geographical entity in the real world.
meaning: When this map feature first went live in Google's geo repository.

name: lastModificationTimestampUs
desc: The timestamp (in microseconds since the UNIX epoch) of the last modification to the feature. Note this includes attachment modifications. The feature's initial creation is also considered as a modification. This is useful for those that consume features via both listening to notifications and reading from repository snapshots. This timestamp can be used to decide whether a feature in the snapshot was already seen in a more recent state through the notifications.
meaning: When the map feature was last modified.

name: removalTimestampUs
desc: The timestamp (in microseconds since the UNIX epoch) of the deletion time of the feature. If the feature is currently removed, this field gets populated with the timestamp the feature first became removed after being live (or being removed from beginning). This field won't be set if the feature is live.
meaning: When the map feature was deleted, if it has been.

name: duplicateOf
desc: If the feature has been marked as a DUPLICATE of another feature, this is the feature ID of that other feature. Note that the other feature may itself be removed. This field is always set.
meaning: Id of the map feature that this one was marked a duplicate of.

name: forwardedId
desc: The feature ID of the forwarded feature. This field is only set in case (3).
meaning: Id of the map feature that this feature's id now forwards to.

name: inactiveDuplicate
desc: If other features have been marked as DUPLICATE of this feature, this is the set of all such feature IDs. All feature IDs in this set should be for removed (aka inactive) features. Note that in the context of historical read requests against MapFacts (when ReadRequest.version_selection.timestamp is set), this field won't be set.
meaning: Ids of removed features that were marked as duplicates of this one.

name: replacedBy
desc: DEPRECATED - Use feature.metadata.feature_replacement_info instead. This field was never populated.
meaning: Deprecated pointer to replacement features that was never actually populated.

name: transitivelyDuplicateOf
desc: If the feature has been transitively marked as a DUPLICATE of another feature (via a chain of size >= 1), this is the feature ID of that other feature which is the end of the chain. The field is always set even if the chain is of size 1. Note that the other feature may itself be removed. This field is only set in case (3).
meaning: The final feature id at the end of a chain of duplicate markings.

name: id
desc: The list of feature IDs. While the exact semantics of these IDs are usage-dependent, the list should never be empty or contain duplicates.
meaning: A plain list of map feature ids.

name: cellId
desc: The S2CellId corresponding to the approximate location of this feature as of when it was first created. This can be of variable accuracy, ranging from the exact centroid of the feature at creation, a very large S2 Cell, or even being completely randomized for locationless features. Cell ids have the nice property that they follow a space-filling curve over the surface of the earth. (See s2cellid.h for details.) WARNING: Clients should only use cell IDs to perform spatial locality optimizations.
meaning: Approximate map cell where a feature sat when created, used for storage locality.

name: fprint
desc: A 64-bit fingerprint used to identify features. Most clients should rely on MapFacts or OneRing to choose fingerprints. If creating new fprints, the strategy should be chosen so that the chance of collision is remote or non-existent, and the distribution should be reasonably uniform. For example, if the source data assigns unique ids to features, then a fingerprint of the provider name, version, and source id is sufficient.
meaning: A 64-bit fingerprint used to identify a map feature.

name: temporaryData
desc: A place for clients to attach arbitrary data to a feature ID. Never set in MapFacts.
meaning: Scratch space for arbitrary client data on a feature id; never set in live map data.

name: bulkUpdatable
desc: This field indicates whether the feature is subject to bulk updates. Caution must be exercised while editing such features since the changes made by the edits will be overwritten by the bulk update (if the feature is bulk updated). See go/mapfacts-abu for more information.
meaning: Whether this feature gets overwritten by bulk data updates.

name: coreVersionToken
desc: core_version_token is an opaque token representing the version of the core fields of the feature. This field is not updated when attachments are changed.
meaning: Opaque version token covering the feature's core fields only.

name: featureReplacementInfo
desc: Metadata for tracking when a feature is derived from or replaced by another feature or set of features.
meaning: Record of when a feature was derived from or replaced by other features.

name: fieldMetadata
desc: Metadata about certain repeated fields and their subfields, for which field type is not granular enough.
meaning: Bookkeeping metadata about certain repeated fields on the feature.

name: forwardings
desc: Feature ID forwardings, if applicable.
meaning: Id forwarding information for this map feature.

name: history
desc: Metadata related to the history.
meaning: Timestamps describing this feature's creation, edit, and removal history.

name: versionToken
desc: version_token is an opaque token representing the version of this feature. It can be used as a concurrency token when sending edits.
meaning: Opaque version token used to detect conflicting edits to a feature.

name: attachmentTypeId
desc: Required when field_type == ATTACHMENT.
meaning: Attachment type id, required when the referenced property is an attachment.

name: attributeId
desc: Required when field_type == FEATURE_ATTRIBUTE.
meaning: Attribute id, required when the referenced property is a feature attribute.

name: kgPropertyId
desc: Required when field_type == KNOWLEDGE_GRAPH_PROPERTY.
meaning: Knowledge Graph property id, required when the property comes from that schema.

name: nameLanguage
desc: RESERVED
meaning: Reserved placeholder field with no described use.

name: geopoliticalGeometry
desc: Geopolitical (unsimplified) polygons for a feature for different geopolitical use cases.
meaning: Unsimplified polygons used for different geopolitical presentations of a place.

name: name
desc: The name(s) of this feature. A feature may have different names in different languages, colloquial or "vanity" names, etc.
meaning: The names of this place, possibly in several languages or as nicknames.

name: relatedTimezone
desc: Contains time zones known to be associated with a feature. Most features are associated with the single time zone that contains them. However, some larger features (countries, continents, etc.) are associated with all of the time zones they contain. Most features can have any number of related time zones, but TYPE_SEGMENT and TYPE_ESTABLISHMENT_POI features can have at most 1.
meaning: Time zones known to be associated with a map feature.

name: storefrontGeometryModel
desc: Geometry Store ID and materialized geometry for a POI feature's storefront(s). IMPORTANT: Clients may not write to this field directly; see go/geometry-store-reading-and-writing#writing-to-geometry-store.
meaning: Stored geometry reference and shape for a place's store front.

name: center
desc: The conceptual center of the feature, used for routing. For cities, this would be the center of the downtown, or maybe the location of city hall. For states and countries it might be the capital city. Most feature types will not have a conceptual center - by default, routing will use the centroid of the feature's geometry. If you need a feature center point consider using GetFeatureGeometryCenter() function from geostore/base/public/feature.h rather than reading from this field directly.
meaning: The conceptual center point of a place, used for routing.

name: displayData
desc: Data used to render this feature on a map.
meaning: Data used to draw this feature on a map.

name: detailed3dModel
desc: Geometry Store ID and materialized geometry representing the feature's physical presence in the world. Like geometry_3d above, but with additional semantic or renderable details, e.g. labeled surfaces ("door", "window"), material specifications, etc. IMPORTANT: Clients may not write to this field directly; see go/geometry-store-reading-and-writing#writing-to-geometry-store.
meaning: Reference to a detailed 3D model of the feature with labeled surfaces and materials.

name: elevationModel
desc: Captures elevation data used on TYPE_DIGITAL_ELEVATION_MODEL features.
meaning: Elevation data carried by digital terrain model features.

name: syntheticGeometry
desc: We prefer features that have geometry over those that do not. In some cases we synthesize geometry (e.g., polygons for postal codes). This flag is set to indicate features that have such synthetic geometry.
meaning: Flag saying the feature's shape was generated by Google rather than sourced.

name: polygonForDisplay
desc: Provide version of the geometry suitable for display. This has been subject to water removal and (possibly) moderate simplification.
meaning: A simplified version of the feature's shape suitable for drawing on a map.

name: geometryPrecisionMeters
desc: If set, the feature's actual location can be assumed to be somewhere within a circle of this radius, centered on the feature's location. More information on this field at go/gpm-definition-update. NOTE: Only applicable to features with 'point' geometry. Please contact geo-schema-team@ if you have non-point use cases for which this field would be useful.
meaning: Radius in meters within which the feature's true location is assumed to fall.

name: accessPoint
desc: Optional access point information. Access points hold detailed information about routing endpoints. For example, the main Google office is at "1600 Amphitheatre Parkway". The feature representing that office has a polygon, a center, and an address with components for the street number, route, locality, etc. The access point information, on the other hand, identifies the specific segment, the latitude/longitude of the driveway, and so forth.
meaning: Routing entry points for a place, such as the exact driveway location.

name: rankDetails
desc: The rank field is computed as a weighted sum of several signals. This field contains a protocol buffer whose fields give those signals and their weights. Clients should try very hard not to depend on these individual signals and use the single rank field instead. At some point in the future, this field will not be exposed anymore.
meaning: The individual signals and weights that were combined into a map feature's rank.

name: metadata
desc: Metadata about this particular feature. Metadata is managed internally by the Geo Data Infrastructure and in general should not be set by clients. Features that don't ultimately come from the Geo repository (MapFacts) won't have any metadata set.
meaning: Internal geo infrastructure metadata about this feature, not set by clients.

name: kgProperty
desc: Properties that apply to this feature whose schema is defined in the Knowledge Graph schema (see
meaning: Knowledge Graph properties attached to this map feature.

name: relatedFeature
desc: Geographic or logical relationships to other features. Importers don't need to fill a geographic relationship in - it is handled by related feature processing by a standalone pipeline. Adding "contained by" country relations is however encouraged (and required for TYPE_ROUTE features). WARNING: Updates to this field handled by standalone pipelines are NOT atomic with regard to updates to the features being referenced; we do not guarantee that a given MapFacts snapshot will be consisten
meaning: Geographic or logical relationships between this map feature and other features.

name: visualizationArea
desc: Geometry Store ID and materialized geometry representing a bounding box of the feature's geometry (or the building/grounds a POI occupies) for stylized rendering, UX experiences, etc. IMPORTANT: Clients may not write to this field directly; see go/geometry-store-reading-and-writing#writing-to-geometry-store.
meaning: A bounding shape of the feature used for stylized map rendering.

name: attachment
desc: The collection of attachments for this feature. Documentation:
meaning: The collection of attachments carried by this map feature.

name: relatedTerminalPoint
desc: Terminal points associated with this feature. For instance, an airport terminal may have specifically designated pickup and drop-off points.
meaning: Pickup and drop-off points associated with a place, such as airport terminals.

name: sourceInfo
desc: A list of the data sources that were used to construct this feature, together with optional "raw data" in the provider's format. Raw data should not be used by production clients but may be useful for exploring data that is not currently converted to a canonical form.
meaning: The data sources used to build this map feature, plus optional raw provider data.

name: futureGeometryFor
desc: Specifies the feature that this feature's geometry will replace. If this field is populated, the referenced feature must have a future_geometry reference back to this feature. This field is only allowed (and required) for TYPE_FUTURE_GEOMETRY features.
meaning: Pointer to the feature whose shape this future-geometry feature will replace.

name: track
desc: Defines the geometry of a feature as a sequence of 6D poses, including lat, lng, altitude, roll, pitch, and yaw. Only lat and lng are typically required. Each track has an index so that they can be viewed in a stable order.
meaning: The feature's shape as a sequence of positions with orientation.

name: businessChain
desc: Data specific to business chain features, e.g., Canonical GConcepts.
meaning: Data specific to business chain features, such as their canonical categories.

name: geometry3d
desc: Geometry Store ID and materialized geometry representing the feature's physical shape in the world. IMPORTANT: Clients may not write to this field directly; see go/geometry-store-reading-and-writing#writing-to-geometry-store.
meaning: Reference to the feature's 3D physical shape in the geometry store.

name: point
desc: Defines the geometry of the feature. The geometry may be specified as an arbitrary union of points, poses, polylines, tracks, and polygons. Points, poses, polylines, and tracks are assumed to represent regions of unspecified size or width rather than regions of zero area. Most features should have some sort of geometry. Geometry may be synthesized if none is available (e.g., polygons for postal codes). The synthetic_geometry flag should be set in that case. Point is currently enforced as a non-r
meaning: Point coordinates defining where the feature sits on the map.

name: transitLineVariant
desc: RESERVED
meaning: Reserved placeholder for transit line variant data.

name: interiorCovering
desc: S2 interior covering that consists of cells completely enclosed within the feature's geometry (for features with polygonal geometry).
meaning: Map cells lying completely inside the feature's polygon.

name: bestLocale
desc: Describes the best-match locale for this feature.
meaning: The locale that best matches this feature, used for choosing names.

name: child
desc: Features can define themselves as a collection of other features. For example, a route is a collection of road segments, and a feature for the "Great Lakes" could be defined as lakes Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie, and Ontario. It is not recommended to design a multi level tree using the child field to build up a feature because it requires fetching many features to see the details of the feature. In practice this is used to model archipelago, route, transit (agencies, lines, trips, d
meaning: Other map features that together make up this feature, such as segments of a route.

name: establishment
desc: Also allowed on TYPE_BUSINESS_CHAIN and TYPE_TRANSIT_AGENCY features, to model the feature's phone number(s). Other fields within EstablishmentProto are not permitted on non-TYPE_ESTABLISHMENT features.
meaning: Business-specific data for a place, such as hours and phone numbers.

name: storefrontGeometry
desc: Represents information about the store front geometry. Only TYPE_ESTABLISHMENT_POI should have this field set.
meaning: The shape of a business's store front.

name: website
desc: The official website of this feature. Stored as a repeated field to allow for multilingual official websites (see comments in url.proto).
meaning: The official website addresses of a place, one per language.

name: propertyValueStatus
desc: The value status of properties on this feature. For example, this specifies whether the feature is known to have no name (this is the value status of the 'FEATURE_NAME' property). Only property IDs which have no specific value are allowed to have a value status. Note: not all field types will be supported, please contact geo schema team if you want to enable this field for a field type that is not currently supported.
meaning: Marks that a map feature is known to have no value for certain properties, such as no name.

name: socialReference
desc: All establishments must have a social reference. WARNING: Aside from creating new establishments, please do NOT introduce new uses; treat social references as if they were deprecated. For alternatives and more, see g3doc/company/teams/gdeng/geo-schema-reference/home/feature-types/establishments/social-reference.md.
meaning: A social reference attached to business listings, treated as deprecated.

name: tollPath
desc: Represents information about /geo/type/toll_path features.
meaning: Details for toll path map features.

name: route
desc: Additional details on the feature types below can be found in the individual protocol buffer definitions. These extensions capture data that is specific to a set of feature types and which makes no sense for other feature types.
meaning: Extra route-specific details attached to route-type map features.

name: parking
desc: Describes parking details for the feature.
meaning: Parking details for this place.

name: knowledgeGraphReference
desc: RESERVED
meaning: Reserved placeholder for a Knowledge Graph reference, with no described use.

name: tollCluster
desc: Represents information about TYPE_TOLL_CLUSTER features.
meaning: Details for toll cluster map features.

name: rawGconceptInstanceContainer
desc: Geo Ontology GConcept Instances - Design doc linked off
meaning: Container holding the raw ontology category instances attached to a map feature.

name: internal
desc: Data for this feature that is less about the feature and more about other data in the feature. For example, it might be data about the rights we have to other data in this FeatureProto, or MapFacts-internal shape IDs for this feature's polygons.
meaning: Internal data about the feature's other data, such as usage rights and shape ids.

name: threeDimModel
desc: Captures full model representing the feature's 3D geometry. Should only be found on TYPE_COMPOUND_BUILDING features for now, but not part of the BuildingProto extension for possible future extensions.
meaning: A full three-dimensional model of the feature's shape.

name: temporaryData
desc: A place for clients to attach arbitrary data to a feature. Never set in MapFacts.
meaning: Scratch space for clients to attach arbitrary data; never set in production map data.

name: originalId
desc: This field is used internally by the pipeline for id stability. It should not be set by individual importers, nor should it be read by consumer clients. In particular, this field will not be present in features read or snapshotted from the Mapfacts Repository.
meaning: Internal pipeline id used for id stability; absent from repository reads.

name: relatedBorder
desc: For TYPE_COUNTRY or TYPE_ADMINISTRATIVE_AREA1 features, this field defines the associated TYPE_BORDERs which reference this feature. The linked TYPE_BORDERs must have the feature.border set, pointing to this feature. TYPE_COUNTRY or TYPE_ADMINISTRATIVE_AREA1 features must have this field set for each TYPE_BORDER referencing them.
meaning: Links a country or administrative area to the border features that reference it.

name: preferredViewport
desc: The preferred viewport for this feature. If present, this latitude-longitude rectangle holds the preferred viewport for the feature. For example, it might hold the bounds of the "central" portion of a large city. There are no aspect ratio requirements. This is an optional field: if no viewport is supplied, interested clients can use heuristics to determine a viewport. Calling the standard GetFeatureGeometryBound() function would be a good way to start but note that it can return an emp
meaning: The preferred map rectangle to show when displaying this feature.

name: futureGeometry
desc: Specifies the TYPE_FUTURE_GEOMETRY whose geometry will replace this feature's geometry. If this field is populated, the referenced future geometry must have a future_geometry_for referencing this feature.
meaning: Pointer to the shape that will replace this feature's shape in the future.

name: exemptRegulatedArea
desc: A list of feature ids of polygon based restrictions that do not apply to this feature. This may only include features of TYPE_REGULATED_AREA that also have a feature.regulated_area.restriction field defined. Setting this field opts the feature out of all restrictions set on that regulated area.
meaning: Regulated areas whose restrictions do not apply to this feature.

name: disputedArea
desc: Represents information about disputed areas. Only TYPE_DISPUTED_AREA features should have the field set.
meaning: Information about disputed territory features.

name: level
desc: Represents information about TYPE_LEVEL features.
meaning: Information about building floor features.

name: operations
desc: Information about this feature's operations, e.g. when this feature is temporarily closed. NOTE: for legacy reasons, some closure-specifc information (e.g. permanent closure reason) lives in ExistenceProto instead. In the future, such information should move here in OperationsProto.
meaning: Information about whether a place is currently operating or temporarily closed.

name: waterRemovedPolygon
desc: A version of the geometry which has water removed but is not simplified (thus having equal or more vertices than polygon_for_display).
meaning: The feature's outline with water removed and no simplification applied.

name: type
desc: The type of this feature -- see comments above.
meaning: The kind of map feature this record describes.

name: pose
desc: Defines the geometry of a feature as a 6D pose, including lat, lng, altitude, roll, pitch, and yaw along the WGS-84 ellipsoid. Only the lat and lng are strictly required.
meaning: Position and orientation of a feature in six dimensions on the earth's ellipsoid.

name: covering
desc: S2 cell coverings for this feature. See util/geometry/s2cell_union.h for more information about S2 cells. Coverings are useful for quick containment or intersection tests. S2 covering that consists of cells that intersect with the feature.
meaning: Map cells that intersect this feature, used for fast containment tests.

name: status
desc: All features can have "existence" information associated with them.
meaning: Information about whether a map feature actually exists.

name: address
desc: Address for this feature. A Geo Schema address is designed to model a mailing address, so only features that have mailing addresses in the real world may have addresses. Each feature should have only one address. If you want to describe the geographic location of a feature which does not have a mailing address with respect to other well-known features, some other schema constructs should be used. Note that the field is defined as repeated though features that use this field with its intended sem
meaning: The mailing address of a map feature.

name: rank
desc: WARNING: Please do NOT introduce new uses of this field; treat it as if it were deprecated. For appropriate ranking contacts, see g3doc/company/teams/gdeng/geo-schema-reference/home/feature-properties/rank.md. A floating-point number between 0.0 and 1.0 indicating how "important" we think this feature is. This can be used to decide which features to render on maps, and how to rank results when the user does a search. The rank can depend on any number of factors such as the number of re
meaning: A 0-to-1 importance score for a map feature, flagged as effectively deprecated.

name: id
desc: The globally unique id for this feature.
meaning: The globally unique id of this map feature.

name: anchoredGeometry
desc: Represents information about the feature’s anchored geometry.
meaning: Information about the feature's anchored 3D geometry.

name: relatedEntrance
desc: Logical relationship to other features that are entrances or exits to this feature.
meaning: Links a place to the features that act as its entrances or exits.

name: bound
desc: A latitude-longitude rectangle used by bucketing MapReduces. See the documentation on bucketing MapReduce for details. This field can be a source of confusion. Because it is called "bound", it is often assumed that it is a tight bound on the geometry but it can be (and often is) much larger. If a tight bound is needed then use the standard GetFeatureGeometryBound() function instead. To be more explicit, if you are using this field for
meaning: A loose latitude-longitude rectangle around a feature used by batch processing jobs.

name: verticalOrdering
desc: Represents vertical ordering for this feature relative to other geometrically-overlaping features. See go/aboutgrades for more information about distinction among different levels.
meaning: How this feature stacks vertically against other overlapping features.

name: derivedFrom
desc: This feature was created to replace other features that are referenced by this field.
meaning: The older map features this feature was created to replace.

name: replacedBy
desc: This feature was replaced by other features that are referenced by this this field.
meaning: The newer map features that replaced this one.

name: featurePropertyId
desc: The feature property id for which this entry tracks rights.
meaning: Identifies which feature property a data-rights entry applies to.

name: minRightsLevel
desc: The minimum rights level among all current values for this feature property id.
meaning: The lowest usage-rights level among the values for a feature property.

name: curvature
desc: RESERVED
meaning: Reserved placeholder for the curvature of a lane flow line.

name: ingredients
desc: Ingredients of the food dish option.
meaning: The ingredients listed for a menu item option.

name: media
desc: Photos of the food dish option.
meaning: Photos of a menu item option.

name: nameInfo
desc: The repeated name_info field here is for item options with names or descriptions listed in multiple languages. When an item option has no names or descriptions, the size of the repeated field name_info may be 0. For example, when a food menu item does not have multiple options, the item option proto is used only to specify price and nutritional information, so it will not have a name_info field. There should be at most one name_info for any given language.
meaning: Names and descriptions of a menu item option in multiple languages.

name: nutritionFacts
desc: Nutrition facts of the food dish option. Note that it also includes calories information with a finer defined unit information.
meaning: Nutrition and calorie information for a menu item option.

name: portionSize
desc: Size of the order, represented in units of items. (e.g. 4 "skewers”, 6 "pieces”)
meaning: How many units the menu item option contains, such as six pieces.

name: preparationMethods
desc: Methods on how the food dish option is prepared.
meaning: How the dish option is prepared.

name: price
desc: We use PriceRangeProto here but we expect the lower_price and upper_price to be both set to equal numbers because an option should have a single price. This field is not required because food item prices may be variable depending on season.
meaning: The price of a menu item option.

name: servesNumPeople
desc: Number of people can be served by this food dish option.
meaning: How many people the dish option serves.

name: nameInfo
desc: The repeated name_info field is for the ingredient in multiple languages.
meaning: The ingredient's name in multiple languages.

name: quantity
desc: Required.
meaning: The number of units in a menu item portion.

name: unit
desc: Required. The repeated name_info field is for the unit in multiple languages.
meaning: The name of the portion unit in multiple languages.

name: nameInfo
desc: The repeated name_info field is for items listed in multiple languages.
meaning: Menu item names listed in multiple languages.

name: gconceptId
desc: The unique identifier of a GConcept (e.g. "gcid:railway").
meaning: The identifier of a place category concept, such as railway.

name: metadata
desc: Field-level metadata for this GConcept.
meaning: Per-field bookkeeping metadata for this category assignment.

name: prominence
desc: The relative prominence of this category to this feature according to the data provider, as one of the values from the enum above. Prominence is a measure of how well the given GConcept describes the feature. An example is a gas station with convenience store and ATM. All three GConcepts are very relevant, but the gas_station GConcept is the most prominent. If the prominence of this GConcept is unknown, this field should not be set.
meaning: How well a given category describes the place, according to the data provider.

name: excludesGeometryOf
desc: Features whose geometry to exclude while composing the geometry of this feature.
meaning: Features whose shapes are subtracted when composing this feature's shape.

name: includesGeometryOf
desc: Features whose geometry to include while composing the geometry of this feature.
meaning: Features whose shapes are combined to build this feature's shape.

name: footprint
desc: Geometry (in STGeography format) materialized from the footprint field of the Geometry Store record associated with the geometry_id referenced above.
meaning: The footprint shape copied from the geometry store record.

name: geometry
desc: Geometry materialized from the full_fidelity_proto field of the Geometry Store record associated with the geometry_id referenced above.
meaning: Full-detail shape copied from the geometry store record.

name: geometryId
desc: The ID of a record in the Geometry Store.
meaning: The identifier of a record in the geometry store.

name: restOfWorldPolygon
desc: The unsimplified, water-subtracted polygon representing the feature's geometry as viewed by the rest of the world, which may differ from its default polygon, for example by excluding certain regions.
meaning: The feature's outline as viewed by the rest of the world.

name: selfPolygon
desc: The unsimplified, water-subtracted polygon representing the feature's geometry as viewed by the country that administers it, which may differ from its default polygon, for example by including disputed areas.
meaning: The feature's outline as viewed by the country that administers it.

name: conveysAttributionTo
desc: If present, some aspect of this feature (usually name or geometry) can signify ownership of the area by the region specified. The string, if present, will be a region code. E.g., suppose a TYPE_POSTAL_CODE feature has a Russian format in Crimea (which is disputed by Ukraine), then this field would be set to "RU".
meaning: Region code whose ownership of an area this feature's name or shape implies.

name: regionSpecificName
desc: Any specific handling of this feature's name from different regions' POVs. This field can only contain up to one name per region/language combination (each of which would be a separate RegionSpecificNameProto).
meaning: Names for this feature that differ depending on the viewing region.

name: regionalPolygonAdjustment
desc: Adjustments to the base polygon of this feature to construct a region-specific view. In general, this field is edited only by go/mf-triggers based on the data written to regional_polygon_composing_claims. This field should only be directly edited if there are region-specific adjustments that cannot be represented using the geometry of this feature's claims, but note that anything written to this field will be overwritten by go/mf-triggers if regional_polygon_composing_claims is ever edited. See
meaning: Shape adjustments used to build a region-specific view of the feature.

name: regionalPolygonComposingClaims
desc: Feature's claim(s) which compose the region-specific polygon. This composition will be used by go/mf-triggers to compose the specified region's view of this feature's geometry. The difference between that polygon and this feature's base polygon will be stored in regional_polygon_adjustment below. Edits to this field will overwrite anything already stored in regional_polygon_adjustment. See go/geopolitical-geometry-schema for more information.
meaning: The territorial claims used to compose a region-specific outline.

name: polygonToAdd
desc: Polygon to add to the feature's base polygon to get the view for the given region. Applied after polygon_to_subtract, such that any region contained in both polygons WILL be part of the final result.
meaning: Area added to a feature's base outline for one region's view.

name: polygonToSubtract
desc: Polygon to subtract from the feature's base polygon to get the view for the given region.
meaning: Area removed from a feature's base outline for one region's view.

name: regionCode
desc: Region code (or other identifier) for the region.
meaning: The region this shape adjustment applies to.

name: regionCode
desc: Region code (or other identifier) for the region.
meaning: The region this set of composing claims applies to.

name: regionExcludedClaims
desc: TYPE_DISPUTED_AREAs claimed by this feature excluded from this region's view of the feature's geometry. (The TDAs must have polygonal geometry and be referenced in this feature's political.claim field.) The polygons of these claims will be subtracted to this feature's base polygon when this feature is viewed from the specified region.
meaning: Disputed areas left out of this region's view of the feature.

name: regionIncludedClaims
desc: TYPE_DISPUTED_AREAs claimed by this feature and included in this region's view of the feature's geometry. (The TDAs must have polygonal geometry and be referenced in this feature's political.claim field.) The polygons of these claims will be added to this feature's base polygon when this feature is viewed from the specified region.
meaning: Disputed areas included in this region's view of the feature.

name: index
desc: The index of the point along the segment, where 0 is the starting point. This means that the index of a point along a segment and its sibling will be different.
meaning: Position of a point along a road segment, counting from the start.

name: level
desc: The grade level of the indexed point. The grade level can be thought of as a relative vertical ordering with respect to other segments at the same point, where larger/more positive numbers are "higher". Negative grade level values are allowed and are typically used for points below grade level (0 is a common choice to represent the level of points at the ground level). For vertical segments, the height, i.e. the vertical length, is represented by difference of levels in millimeters. Fo
meaning: Relative vertical level of a point on a road, where higher numbers sit above.

name: text
desc: Zero or more texts of the specified type, in various languages. If this is a HTML_DESCRIPTION blob then these texts would hold the description in English, German, and so forth. The text is an HTML fragment, not a full page. The fragment should be suitable for including in a DIV. It must have balanced HTML tags. It may use HTML's "class" attributes to assign classes to HTML elements. This allows the HTML to be formatted by an (external) style sheet. The HTML should not have embedded sty
meaning: HTML description text for a map feature in one or more languages.

name: definesGeometryFor
desc: Features whose geometry depends on this feature's geometry.
meaning: Other features whose shape depends on this feature's shape.

name: geometryComposition
desc: Features whose geometry defines the geometry of this feature (i.e. "composing features").
meaning: The features whose shapes together define this feature's shape.

name: polygonShapeId
desc: A unique identifier for this feature's polygon data which is being held externally in Shapestore (see go/shapestore).
meaning: Identifier for this feature's outline held in an external shape store.

name: restOfWorldPolygonShapeId
desc: A unique identifier for this feature's rest-of-world view polygon data which is being held externally in Shapestore (see go/shapestore). This is part of the feature's geopolitical geometry.
meaning: Identifier for the rest-of-world view of this feature's outline in external storage.

name: rightsStatus
desc: Per-field rights for this feature. See
meaning: Per-field data usage rights for this map feature.

name: selfPolygonShapeId
desc: A unique identifier for this feature's self view polygon data which is being held externally in Shapestore (see go/shapestore). This is part of the feature's geopolitical geometry.
meaning: Identifier for the self-view of this feature's outline in external storage.

name: trust
desc: Trust signals/annotations for the feature. In an input feature, these signals are computed at the beginning of the pipeline and are immutable during the processing. In output features, this proto may define the rules/criteria that a newer edit should meet, in order to be applied.
meaning: Trust annotations computed for a map feature during data processing.

name: waterRemovedPolygonShapeId
desc: A unique identifier for this feature's water-removed polygon data which is being held externally in Shapestore (see go/shapestore).
meaning: Identifier for the water-removed version of this feature's outline in external storage.

name: isAuto
desc: Whether or not the piece of data has been generated automatically (i.e., by a bot/automated process based on heuristics/algorithms rather than coming as a fact set by some human user or data provider based on their knowledge). Note that this does NOT imply that the value was set as a result of a bot operation on the repository, since it is conceivable to use a bot/automated process simply as a way of convenience to ingest large amount of canonical/ground truth data.
meaning: Whether this piece of map data was generated automatically rather than by a person.

name: sourceSummary
desc: Information about the source providing the piece of data this metadata is attached to.
meaning: Information about which source supplied this piece of map data.

name: disallowedConnections
desc: A list of lane connections that are explicitly not allowed to be added. NOTE: This should never reference existing lane connections on this segment.
meaning: Lane connections that must not be added to this road segment.

name: disallowedPrimaryConnection
desc: A list of lane connections which cannot have the primary_connection bit set.
meaning: Lane connections that cannot be marked as the primary connection.

name: travelAllowance
desc: The set of restrictions that apply to this segment; these are actually
meaning: The set of travel restrictions that apply to a road segment.

name: fromLaneNumber
desc: The lane number on this segment.
meaning: The lane number on this road segment.

name: segment
desc: This reference to the other segment is weak, since strong would blow up bounds of all segments.
meaning: A loose pointer to the other road segment in a lane connection.

name: toLaneNumber
desc: This is the lane number on the target segment.
meaning: The lane number on the target road segment.

name: dataset
desc: Within the above provider, the dataset from which this piece of data was generated. For fields that are auto-generated the "dataset" is likely to be some algorithm's or program's name. Similar to SourceInfoProto.dataset but with the difference that it is required to always be set. Providers that don't have a concept of dataset may use "default".
meaning: The dataset within a provider that produced this piece of map data.

name: provider
desc: The data provider from which this piece of data was generated. Equivalent to SourceInfoProto.provider in the public schema.
meaning: The data provider that supplied this piece of map data.

name: childGroup
desc: All artifact intersection groups that are in this logical group.
meaning: Intersection groups contained within this logical group.

name: intersection
desc: The list of TYPE_INTERSECTION features that form this intersection group, but are NOT in any of this group's child groups. This could be an empty list, though that is sub-optimal. Even an empty list would allow the paint team to draw a label for a named intersection, but a non-empty list would, for example, enable PathFinder to generate better directions. Each of the TYPE_INTERSECTION feature referred here must refer back to this feature in its IntersectionProto.
meaning: The intersections that make up this intersection group.

name: parentGroup
desc: Parent logical intersection group. An artifact group that does not have an associated parent logical group is assumed to be both an artifact and logical group.
meaning: The parent logical group of this intersection group.

name: intersectionGroup
desc: The artifact or logical intersection group to which this intersection belongs. If present, the intersection group must also refer back to the intersection. If an intersection is within both the artifact and logical group, then this reference should be to the artifact group.
meaning: The group that this intersection belongs to.

name: outSegment
desc: RESERVED
meaning: Reserved placeholder for outgoing segments at an intersection.

name: segment
desc: The list of segments that terminate at this intersection, in any order. Note that all segments are directed towards the intersection, i.e. their endpoints indicate what sort of intersection this is. This should not be empty because an intersection with no associated segment is meaningless.
meaning: The road segments that end at this intersection.

name: tollCluster
desc: The toll cluster to which this intersection belongs. If present, the toll cluster must also refer back to the intersection. To set this field, the intersection must be a gcid:toll_intersection feature.
meaning: The toll cluster that this intersection belongs to.

name: duration
desc: Describes how much time the service is going to take, e.g. how long it takes to do a haircut. Value of seconds must be from +60 (1 min) to +31,536,000 (365 days) inclusive. Value of nanos must be zero.
meaning: How long a service job is expected to take.

name: jobRelatedCategories
desc: Represents the name of a potential grouping of items. For TYPE_JOB, this is the category names of the categories that a user picked this job type from at the time of input.
meaning: The category names a user picked a job type from.

name: jobTypeId
desc: Unique identifier for a job. This is required for standard jobs and blank for free-form jobs. Job type ids are prefixed with "job_type_id:". Notice this is a unique string representation of a job across languages. E.g., “job_type_id:air_duct_repair”. The existence of a job_type_id means the job type is a standard one, and has a corresponding entry in the Standard Jobs Taxonomy.
meaning: Unique identifier for a standard service job type.

name: jobTypeMid
desc: Represents the MID corresponding to the job_category entity in the Knowledge Graph. For example, job_type_id="job_type_id:install_faucet", job_type_mid="/g/11hzzxjv3f".
meaning: The Knowledge Graph entity identifier for a job category.

name: name
desc: Category name in the primary language of the feature. Generally intended to be used as a fallback when we are unable to fetch the name in the user's language.
meaning: The job category name in the place's main language.

name: id
desc: KG Identifier (MID). For details, see
meaning: A Knowledge Graph entity identifier.

name: featureType
desc: The type of the landmark feature. Allowed types: - TYPE_CARTOGRAPHIC e.g. a putting green or water hazard - TYPE_COMPOUND e.g. - the Empire state building (TYPE_COMPOUND_BUILDING) - a park (TYPE_COMPOUND_GROUNDS) - a section of a retail store (TYPE_COMPOUND_SECTION) - TYPE_ESTABLISHMENT e.g. - the Eiffel Tower (TYPE_ESTABLISHMENT_BUILDING) - a sports field (TYPE_ESTABLISHMENT_GROUNDS) - Starbucks (TYPE_ESTABLISHMENT_POI) - TYPE_INTERSECTION_GROUP e.g. a major intersection - TYPE_NATURAL_FEATURE
meaning: The kind of map feature a landmark is, such as a building or intersection.

name: landmark
desc: The feature ID of the landmark feature.
meaning: The identifier of the landmark feature being referenced.

name: travelMode
desc: The mode(s) of travel for which this landmark is useful.
meaning: Which modes of travel this landmark is useful for.

name: barrierMaterials
desc: If this is a physical barrier marker, represent materials found on the marker.
meaning: Materials found on a physical road barrier marker.

name: crossingPattern
desc: Pattern border and color for crossing markers. These include crosswalks, stop, and yield lines.
meaning: The pattern and color of crosswalk, stop and yield line markings.

name: linearPattern
desc: Stripe pattern, spacing, and color for longitudinal markers.
meaning: The stripe pattern, spacing and color of lane line markings.

name: boundingMarker
desc: References to any gcid:physical_lane_marker features that bound this lane.
meaning: The painted markers that bound a lane.

name: conjoinedCategory
desc: If the current lane is part of a merge/split area, indicates the type (split or merge) and whether the current lane is on the left or right or in the middle of the merge/split area, as seen in the direction of traffic. See go/lane-split-merge-schema
meaning: Whether the lane is part of a merge or split, and on which side.

name: distanceToNextLane
desc: Gap between this lane and the next in meters. This is relevant when the divider is physical, or a wide painted area. For regular painted single or double lines, there is no gap. This distance is duplicated between the innermost lanes for each side. Note that this is not used to describe smallish islands - this is only for long-running gaps. In particular, this models the median width, the gap between HOV lanes/regular lanes on freeways, and the road verge between a curb and sidewalk. Note on spl
meaning: Gap in meters between this lane and the next one.

name: flow
desc: The most logical path for the center of an object to travel along within the lane. Typically, this is the lane's center line, but doesn't have to be.
meaning: The path an object would follow down the middle of a lane.

name: laneConnection
desc: Connections to lanes of other segments at the end of this segment. These connections model the connectivity where you don't have to do a lane change maneuver. If any lane connection is present, assume that all others are forbidden. Also note that segment level restrictions do apply if present, and can disallow some turn even if the lanes are connected. For instance, this can happen with timed or vehicle type based restrictions on the segment. If lane connectivity implies a segment-level restrict
meaning: Which lanes on following road segments this lane connects to.

name: laneDividerCrossing
desc: clang-format on Whether the divider to the inside of this lane can be crossed. Note that we assume this is symmetric, and that this also describes whether someone in the next inside lane can cross to this one. The "inside" lane is the one with a lower lane_number. Note on lane markers: We do not model the painting, but only the resulting legality. There are many painted marker styles and colors that lead to the same legality. We expect Paint or Driveabout to render lanes stylized, with
meaning: Whether the divider on the inner side of the lane may be crossed.

name: laneFollowsSegmentBeginFraction
desc: These indicate for what portion of the segment the lane's flowline exactly follows the segment, and the lane is of constant width. This will be set to not include the whole segment where there is a split/turn/merge at either end of the lane. The painting of the lane should completely synthesize the lane geometry outside of this portion, connecting it to neighboring lanes to make graphical nice.
meaning: Where along the road segment the lane exactly follows the road at constant width.

name: laneNumber
desc: Lanes are numbered from inside of the road outward, i.e. the lane next to the center line is lane 0. The lanes then stack outwards, towards the side that one drives on this segment (right or left). NOTE: do NOT use the lane_number as index for lookup. Lane_number is not guaranteed to match the segment.lane repeated field index.
meaning: The lane's position number, counting outward from the center line.

name: laneToken
desc: A token that can be used to identify the version of the data about this lane.
meaning: A token identifying the version of this lane's data.

name: metadata
desc: Field-level metadata for this lane.
meaning: Per-field bookkeeping metadata for this lane.

name: restriction
desc: Restrictions that apply to this lane only. Examples include HOV lanes. If a lane restriction implies a segment-level restriction (can't route on the segment at all), that restriction will also exist as a segment level restriction. In effect - PathFinder does not have to look at lane restrictions to figure out segment restrictions.
meaning: Restrictions that apply only to this lane, such as carpool rules.

name: shared
desc: True if this lane is usable in both directions (left-turn lane, reversing lane, one-lane road, etc). To get the total number of lanes for a road, add up the lanes in each direction counting 0.5 for each shared lane.
meaning: Whether the lane can be used in both directions.

name: stopLine
desc: References to any gcid:physical_lane_marker features that intersect this lane, with the implication that a moving vehicle should stop there.
meaning: Markers crossing the lane where a vehicle is expected to stop.

name: surface
desc: clang-format on LINT.ThenChange(//depot/google3/geostore/base/proto/segment.proto) Unlike the surface in SegmentProto, this field does not have a default value. This is because the lane-level surface overrides the segment-level surface. The lane's surface should be unset unless explicitly overriding the segment's surface.
meaning: The lane's road surface, overriding the segment's surface.

name: type
desc: clang-format on
meaning: The lane's type.

name: width
desc: Width of this lane in meters. In many cases, we will collect this data by dividing the total road width by the number of lanes. On accuracy: This is a rough average width along this segment. If and when we wanted to be more accurate, we'd extend this schema to have full polygons for segments/lanes rather than just this average width.
meaning: Average width of the lane in meters.

name: boundingMarker
desc: References to any gcid:physical_lane_marker features that bound this lane connection.
meaning: Painted markers that bound this lane connection.

name: connectionToken
desc: A token that can be used to identify the version of the data about this lane connection.
meaning: A token identifying the version of this lane connection's data.

name: curve
desc: Specifies how the flowline should be synthesized in this connection region. If unspecified, heuristics may be used to pick a sweep shape based on retraction values or neighboring curves.
meaning: How the path through a lane connection should be shaped.

name: flow
desc: The most logical path for the center of an object to travel along within the lane connection. Typically, this is the lane connection's center line, but doesn't have to be.
meaning: The path an object would follow through a lane connection.

name: laneNumber
desc: This is the lane number on the target segment. This field is not set if the target segment doesn't have lanes, or we don't know the exact connectivity.
meaning: The lane number on the target segment of a connection.

name: primaryConnection
desc: True if this connects to the unique, natural continuation of the current lane. At most one LaneConnection per lane can have this field set true. This attribute is of interest to ADAS providers as a hint to which lane a vehicle is likely to follow, in the absence of other information about the vehicle's planned path.
meaning: Whether this connection is the natural continuation of the lane.

name: segment
desc: This reference to the other segment is weak, since strong would blow up bounds of all segments.
meaning: A loose pointer to the target road segment of a lane connection.

name: yieldToOtherConnections
desc: The inverse of the primary connection bit that provides a hint that this connection is part of a merge and a vehicle following this connection should yield to vehicles following other incoming connections.
meaning: Whether vehicles following this connection should yield when merging.

name: language
desc: The external form of a Google International Identifiers Initiative (III) LanguageCode object. See google3/i18n/identifiers/languagecode.h for details. We place extra restrictions on languages in addition to what the III library requires. See
meaning: The language code that a piece of tagged text is written in.

name: text
desc: The text (UTF-8 encoding).
meaning: The text content, encoded in UTF-8.

name: building
desc: The building(s) to which this level belongs. A level will typically belong to a single building, but it is valid for a single level to be shared by multiple buildings (for example, a large underground parking lot). These buildings refer back to the level via another strong reference (the BuildingProto.level field).
meaning: The buildings that this floor level belongs to.

name: number
desc: The elevation of this level relative to the ground level, in levels. 0 = ground floor (even in locales that call the ground floor "1st floor"); 0.5 = between ground and first floor, eg mezzanine; 1 = first floor (one level above ground floor); -3 = three levels below ground floor.
meaning: Which floor a level is, relative to the ground floor.

name: line
desc: A linear marker may consist of one or more parallel physical lines. These are ordered left to right along the direction of the marker core polyline.
meaning: The parallel painted lines that make up a road marker.

name: language
desc: The language associated with this preference. The external form of a Google International Identifiers Initiative (III) LanguageCode object. See google3/i18n/identifiers/languagecode.h for details. We place extra restrictions on languages in addition to what the III library requires. See
meaning: A language associated with a locale.

name: official
desc: Flag to indicate if the associated language is "official" within a locale.
meaning: Whether a language is official within a locale.

name: preference
desc: This value represents the preference of the associated language within a locale. It must be between 0.0 and 1.0.
meaning: How preferred a language is within a locale, on a 0 to 1 scale.

name: speakingPercent
desc: Percentage of population that can speak the associated language within a locale. It must be between 0 and 100.
meaning: Share of a locale's population that can speak the language.

name: writingPercent
desc: Percentage of population that can write the associated language within a locale. It must be between 0 and 100.
meaning: Share of a locale's population that can write the language.

name: language
